title: Release 0.11.4: export the callback signature helpers from the package index
body:
## Summary

`v0.11.3` is tagged at `c50d968` and `package.json` still reads `0.11.3`, so this is a bump-then-tag release. One commit has landed on `main` since:

| Commit | Issues / PRs | What it fixes / adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `13e25b3` | #272, #273 | Exports `signCallbackUrl`, `verifyCallbackSignature`, `redactCallbackSignature`, `SIGNATURE_PARAM`, `EXPIRY_PARAM` and `DEFAULT_TTL_MS` from the package index under `utils` |

## Resolution analysis: why 0.11.4 and not 0.12.0

The change is purely additive: new named exports on `utils`, no signature or behaviour change to anything already exported. The callback signing and redaction behaviour itself shipped unchanged in `v0.11.3` (#265, #266); this release only widens what a consumer can reach without deep-importing `src/utils/callbackSignature.cjs`.

The precedent is settled: this repository reserves the minor bump for breaking changes (#221 for 0.9.0, #243 for 0.10.0, #252 for 0.11.0). This is not one, so it is a patch.

It matters in practice: the consuming microservice verifies what this package signs, in the same process, and could not reach `verifyCallbackSignature` without reaching past the package's declared surface.

## Implementation plan

1. Branch `chore/release-0.11.4`; bump `package.json` to `0.11.4`. Nothing else encodes the version.
2. Gates: `yarn test`, `yarn lint`, `yarn validate`.
3. Open the bump PR closing this issue, merge into `main`.
4. Tag `v0.11.4` on `main`, push the tag, and create the GitHub release.

No registry publish; consumers pin by git tag.

## Not in this release

**#3** - the PIM adapter, still blocked on a `headless-pim` spec that exists nowhere. It is the only other open issue in the tracker.
